title: Design System: Dreamlike Canopy Terminal System

body.purpose: All shell output, labels, and prompt content.

components.name: Terminal Surface
components.description: One continuous terminal field; atmospheric depth comes from blur and opacity, never cards.
components.css: .ds-terminal { background: #07110F; color: #D9E6E3; padding: 14px 18px; font: 400 14px/1.4 'Geist Mono', monospace; }

components.name: Directory Capsule
components.css: .ds-directory { background: #24514D; color: #D9E6E3; padding: 0 1ch; font: 400 14px/1.4 'Geist Mono', monospace; }

narrative.overview: Dreamlike Canopy treats the terminal as a quiet instrument panel inside a living forest. Dark mode is a deep blue-green canopy; light mode opens into a misty glade. The interface remains one continuous surface, with semantic ANSI roles carrying status rather than decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Deep forest teal paired with a pale glade companion.
Shared ANSI semantics across automatic appearance switching.
Geist Mono at a stable 14px reading size.
Full paths with an optional compact prompt preset for split panes.

rules.name: Shared Semantics Rule
rules.body: A light/dark switch may change the actual color, but never the meaning of an ANSI role.

rules.name: Risk Signal Rule
rules.body: Coral marks destructive Git states, sunlight marks attention, and canopy green marks positive progress.

rules.name: One-Surface Rule
rules.body: Keep the terminal visually continuous; do not introduce floating cards or decorative glass containers.

dos: Do preserve automatic light/dark theme pairing.
Do use ANSI roles for semantic prompt feedback.
Do maintain the 4.5 minimum-contrast guard in both themes.
donts: Don't introduce a separate light-mode Starship configuration.
Don't use neon accents, gradient text, or decorative glass UI.
Don't change ANSI meaning between Canopy and Glade.
